clue.text: Stumbled, proceeding from one hill to another

parts.note: a fell is a hill or moor in northern England
a down is a rolling chalk hill in southern England

explanation.surface: A walker trips while making their way between two hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proceeding from ... to' sets the two hills in order, FELL first and then DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall down is to stumble and hit the ground, a plain phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Unreliable female has little for small children

parts.note: ickle is baby talk for little

explanation.surface: A capricious woman barely has anything for her kids.
explanation.walkthrough: ICKLE is British nursery talk for 'little'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fickle person changes their mind often and cannot be relied on.

clue.text: Animal tethered by guerrilla, maybe

indicators.note: tethered by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A beast held on a rope by an insurgent, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A llama is a South American animal related to the camel.

clue.text: Sketch pad may be thus used

definitions.text: Sketch pad may be thus used

parts.words: Sketch pad may be thus used
parts.note: a pad is literally marked with a pencil, and something used as a resource is said to be tapped this way

explanation.surface: How an artist's sketchbook gets used up.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means both 'marked with drawings' and 'used as a resource'.
explanation.definitionFit: Resources that are used are said to be tapped this way, and a sketch pad is literally drawn upon.

clue.text: Fancy alternative title for many a quiz show?

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of surprise, as in 'Well, fancy that!'

definitions.text: alternative title for many a quiz show?
definitions.meaning: a quiz show is a test of how much its contestants have learnt

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a cry of surprise like 'fancy that', and a fitting name for any general-knowledge quiz.

clue.text: A bit sweet

definitions.meaning: a ... is a small amount, as in 'a ... tired'
a British pudding of sponge, custard, fruit and cream

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a small amount, and a layered British dessert.

clue.text: Be taught new skills for working on public transport

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a train is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: Learning a new trade so as to work on the railways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for working' only links; RE is the Latin-derived 'on the subject of'.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrain is to learn new skills, often for a different job.

clue.text: With no commitments, have inclination to tour west coast

indicators.note: to tour is to go around, so the free and heel pieces travel round west

parts.note: free means unattached, with no commitments
to heel is to lean or tilt, as a ship does

explanation.surface: An unattached traveller fancies a trip round the western seaboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coast' looks like the seaside but is the verb, the definition; 'to tour' has the first two pieces travel round west.
explanation.definitionFit: To freewheel is to coast along without pedalling or using power.

clue.text: Writer, for example, is included among the elite when book is out

indicators.note: the example and is pieces are set inside the elite word
is out means the book letter leaves the elite word

parts.note: the best are the elite
say is used to mean for example

explanation.surface: A writer joins the top set once a certain book comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out' with 'book' drops B, leaving EST, and 'included among' sets the example and 'is' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayist is a writer of essays, a particular kind of writer.

clue.text: Domestic employee standing at a stop caught bus

parts.note: a char is a British cleaning woman
to ban something is to stop it
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cleaner waits at a stop and catches the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing at' just links the pieces. The bus stop picture hides that 'stop' gives BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old-fashioned motor coach used for outings, so a kind of bus.

clue.text: Harvested brassica plant that met required standards

definitions.meaning: a mustard crop that has been reaped
came up to scratch, was good enough

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be good enough, and read literally describes reaping a mustard crop.

clue.text: Force fails to open lock

indicators.note: the force word does not open, so its first letter is dropped

parts.note: stress is a force acting on a body

explanation.surface: Someone pushes hard against a lock that will not open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to open' removes the opening S of STRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a lock of hair, a synonym in its hair sense.

clue.text: Literati principally merited such a description?

definitions.text: Literati principally merited such a description?

indicators.note: principally means take the leading letter of Literati

parts.note: to have merited something is to have earned it

explanation.surface: A query whether the literary set really deserve to be called scholarly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the literati are fittingly described as scholarly.
explanation.definitionFit: Literati are well-read people, and well-read people are scholarly, which is what this word means.

clue.text: Transport system runs on time, American-style

indicators.note: runs comes on, meaning after, the time letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a way is a manner or style of doing things

explanation.surface: A transit network keeps to schedule, the way Americans run things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American-style' looks like one adjective but splits into two separate pieces; 'on' puts runs after time.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramway is a network of rails along which trams run, a transport system.

clue.text: Mark once converted by these people unwelcome in temple?

definitions.text: Mark once converted by these people unwelcome in temple?

parts.words: Mark once converted by these people unwelcome in temple?
parts.note: the Deutschmark, a former currency, would be exchanged by the traders Jesus drove out of the Temple

explanation.surface: A question about who would have exchanged old German currency, and who was thrown out of the Temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like the gospel writer, but it is the old German currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Currency traders swap one coinage for another, and in the gospels they were driven from the Temple.

clue.text: Mere mortals about to disappear, tossed in whirlpool

indicators.note: to disappear means the about letters vanish from the pool of fodder
tossed means the remaining letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Ordinary people, about to vanish, are flung into a vortex.
explanation.walkthrough: From MERE MORTALS take RE ('about', 'to disappear') and 'tossed' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, originally one off the Norwegian coast.

clue.text: Drug wasted? That's a blow

parts.note: an upper is a stimulant drug
cut is slang for drunk, wasted

explanation.surface: A drug addict, out of it, gets punched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a punch thrown upward at the chin, a kind of blow.

clue.text: Criminal locates impure gold, perhaps

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are crooked and need setting straight

explanation.surface: A villain tracks down some adulterated gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges LOCATES IMPURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is one example of a costly metal like silver or platinum.

clue.text: LA film shot with English celebrity of sorts

indicators.note: shot means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles movie made with a British star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like filming, but it rearranges LA FILM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill fame is notoriety, a bad kind of renown or celebrity.

clue.text: Account written up about old soldier

indicators.note: about means going round, so the reversed account wraps round old
in a down clue, written up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a report is an account

explanation.surface: A report is drafted about a veteran soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' reverses REPORT to TROPER, and 'about' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private soldier in a cavalry or armoured regiment.

clue.text: Lord shouts out, seizing power

indicators.note: seizing means the shouts word grabs power and holds it inside

parts.note: to shout out is to cry out

explanation.surface: A lord yells while grabbing control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord' is the exclamation, as in 'Good Lord!', not a peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, so the mild oath matches 'Lord!'.

clue.text: Foreign character makes one's lip curl

indicators.note: to curl is to twist, so the letters of the fodder are bent into a new order

parts.note: the word one's gives its letters, the S included

explanation.surface: A sneer from someone made to look like a foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curl' rearranges ONES and LIP; here the 's of one's supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a character from a foreign script.

clue.text: Destructive person causing a flap

definitions.meaning: someone who ruins things for others
a hinged panel on an aircraft wing that cuts lift

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: one who ruins things, and an aircraft's lift-reducing flap.

clue.text: Book slightly too big for this shelf

indicators.note: the book is one letter too long for the shelf word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a ledger is an account book

explanation.surface: A book a little too large to fit on this shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly too big for this' says the answer is LEDGER less one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow shelf, as on a wall or window.

clue.text: Scoundrel, one brought before a court

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A villain and an accomplice are hauled up before the judges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought before' just places the pieces in a row ahead of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Curia is the papal court and administration in Rome, and once a Roman court.

clue.text: Finished in warm clothing

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday idioms: completed, and dressed snugly for the cold.

clue.text: Fiddle without piano is less spirited

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the less spirited word goes around piano

parts.note: tamer means more docile, less spirited
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A violin with no piano accompaniment sounds flatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means outside: P goes inside TAMER.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamper with something is to fiddle with or interfere with it.

clue.text: Decorators notice colour's initially wanting in parts of room

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the room parts

parts.note: corners are parts of a room

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of colour's

explanation.surface: Painters spot that the corners of the room lack colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colour's initially' gives C, and 'wanting' takes it from CORNERS to leave ORNERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who adorn things decorate them, so they are decorators.
